Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front: we can apply credits retroactively in most cases, and we can split credits across sub-accounts when they are all under the same billing profile — with a couple of caveats. Details below so your finance team can reconcile.

Retroactive application (May/June):
- We can issue a credit memo that offsets consumption during prior billing periods (this becomes a credit line on your next invoice). We do not rewrite historic invoices unless a tax/legal issue requires it.
- If you require a negative invoice for your accounting workflow, we can generate one, but that will be treated as a separate document and may have different tax formatting depending on jurisdiction.

Portability across sub-accounts: 
- Credits are issued against the billing profile. If you already have sub-accounts configured under the same billing profile we can allocate credits to individual sub-accounts at redemption time.
- If the startups are on separate billing profiles we will need a signed billing addendum to transfer or split credits across profiles.

I'll loop in Marissa from Partnerships for program-level mechanics and Priyom for billing/invoice language.

Next steps: can you share a short CSV with the sub-account IDs and the May/June usage rows you want us to apply credits to? If finance wants a negative invoice instead of a credit memo please flag that explicitly.

Cheers,

Hi all —

Attached are two short artifacts I prepared per Marissa's ask: 1) credit_memo_template (PDF) and 2) negative_invoice_example (PDF). Short summary of the controls and practical differences: 

- Credit memo: preferred in ~95% of cases. It posts as a line item on the next invoice and carries a reference to the original usage period. For US customers this is typically non-taxable (reduces taxable sales), but in the EU some countries treat credit memos differently — we include a "reversal reason" code and maintain the original invoice reference.

- Negative invoice: creates a standalone document that the customer can process as a distinct accounting transaction. It can be cleaner for some sponsors' internal workflows but may require additional tax registration details if the sponsor expects a VAT reversal.

- Splitting credits across sub-accounts: operationally we create an allocation token tied to your billing profile. The CSV you provide should include: sub-account-id, desired-credit-amount, original-usage-period, invoice-ref (if available). Once we receive that, we apply allocations and issue the credit memo(s). If the sponsors want transfer across billing profiles we need a signed billing addendum (I can attach a short one-page addendum for signature).

I've attached the two PDFs and a draft invoice (draft-invoice-seedwave-LLA.pdf) showing how the credit line will appear. SeedWave finance is CC'd for visibility — please confirm they have what they need.
